content.value_statement: EUDR reviews require coordinated product, supplier, and sourcing evidence. This guide helps your assistant draft applicability decisions, supplier checklists, and due diligence documentation for professional review.
actual_capabilities: Guides applicability reviews covering product scope, company role, size class, and relevant dates.
Supports draft product mapping to Annex I CN codes for verification against current official lists.
Outlines Due Diligence Statement content using the Annex II structure.
Guides supplier geolocation checklists covering coordinate formats and legality evidence per plot.
Frames supply chain risk assessments using country benchmarks and Article 10 criteria.
limitations: The folder contains a public guide only; original scripts, extension source, and templates are not included.
Outputs are drafts, not legal advice or proof of regulatory compliance.
Dates, amendments, country benchmarks, and CN mappings require verification against current official sources.
The skill does not submit Due Diligence Statements to TRACES or independently verify supplier evidence.

use_cases.title: Review Importer Applicability
use_cases.description: Organize product scope, operator role, and missing evidence before preparing an EUDR due diligence file.
use_cases.target_user: Coffee and cocoa import compliance teams

use_cases.title: Assess Downstream Obligations
use_cases.description: Draft a review of downstream roles and potential reliefs, identifying legal assumptions requiring verification.

use_cases.title: Request Supplier Plot Evidence
use_cases.description: Prepare supplier requests for geolocation data, coordinate formats, and plot-level legality evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Check Initial Applicability
prompt_templates.prompt: We import coffee from Brazil into the EU. Draft an EUDR applicability review and list missing information. Flag legal claims requiring current official verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish scope and information needs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Supplier Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these supplier details: [details], draft a geolocation and legality evidence checklist. Separate available evidence from missing data and unverified claims.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Statement Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this product and sourcing evidence: [evidence], draft an Annex II Due Diligence Statement outline. Mark missing fields and assumptions. Do not submit anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a statement for review and manual submission.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Supply Chain Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these supply chains: [details]. Draft Article 10 risk assessments using supplied official country benchmarks. Explain provisional conclusions, evidence gaps, and required mitigation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: compare documented risk conclusions across supply chains.

output_examples.input: We import coffee from Brazil into the EU. What should our initial EUDR review cover?
output: Draft scope review: check the product CN code against the current Annex I.
Role review: assess whether the company acts as an operator based on the transaction.
Evidence needed: company size, transaction details, supplier records, and plot geolocation.
Next step: verify applicable dates and current country benchmarks before finalizing the assessment.

output_examples.input: Create a supplier checklist for a cocoa shipment with missing plot coordinates.
output: Missing evidence: geolocation for each production plot.
Supplier request: provide plot identifiers, coordinates, and relevant legality evidence.
Review task: validate coordinate formats and confirm plot coverage.
Status: due diligence draft remains incomplete until required evidence is reviewed.

best_practices: Provide product descriptions, CN codes, company role, and sourcing details before requesting an applicability assessment.
Verify regulatory dates, product scope, and country benchmarks against current official sources.
Keep evidence traceable to each supply chain and obtain professional review before submission.
anti_patterns: Treating a generated draft as legal advice or a guarantee of compliance.
Accepting country risk labels or CN mappings without checking current official lists.
Assuming a completed outline means supplier evidence was verified or a statement was submitted.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides a public guide for drafting EUDR applicability reviews, supplier checklists, statement outlines, and supply chain risk assessments.

faq.question: Does it include executable tools or packaged templates?
faq.answer: No. The guide explicitly states that original scripts, extension source, and templates are not included in this folder.

faq.question: Does it submit statements to TRACES?
faq.answer: No. It helps draft statement content, but users must review and submit the data themselves.

faq.question: Are its regulatory details guaranteed to be current?
faq.answer: No. Verify dates, amendments, CN codes, and country benchmarks against current official sources before relying on an assessment.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide product descriptions, available CN codes, company size and role, sourcing countries, supplier records, and plot geolocation evidence.

faq.question: Can the output replace legal review?
faq.answer: No. Outputs are structured drafts and need professional review before use in compliance decisions.
